title: On the Coastal Road
reader_question: Who rode with the Prophet ﷺ and Abu Bakr after the cave, and what happened on the road by the sea?

overview.text: After three nights hidden in the cave, the camels came at last, and with them the man who would show the way. Four riders set out: two of them hunted men, one a freed slave, and one a guide who did not share their faith. He led them down to the sea. On the road, strangers who knew Abu Bakr asked him about the man riding in front of him, and one blazing noon a long rock offered shade. But the pursuit had not ended in Makkah.

paragraphs.text: People knew Abu Bakr. His hair had turned grey, and he had often passed among the people of Madinah on his trading journeys; the Prophet ﷺ, whose hair had not greyed, they did not know. In fact, the Prophet ﷺ was the older of the two, by more than two years. Men would meet them and ask, "Abu Bakr, who is this man in front of you?" "This man guides me on the way," he would answer. Whoever heard it thought he meant the road. He meant the way of good. The Prophet ﷺ had told Abu Bakr, "Keep people busy away from me, for a prophet should not lie," and when they asked who was with him, Abu Bakr said, "A guide who guides me."

paragraphs.text: Years later, Abu Bakr told the story of one day on that road. He had bought a camel saddle from ‘Azib for thirteen dirhams, and ‘Azib would not let his son al-Bara carry it home until Abu Bakr told them how he and the Prophet ﷺ had fared when they went out with the idolaters hunting them. "Watchers had been set for us," Abu Bakr said, "so we went out by night."

paragraphs.text: They pressed on through the night and the next day, until the sun stood at its height and the road lay empty, with no one passing on it. Abu Bakr cast his eyes about for any shade to shelter in, and a long rock rose into view, with shade the sun had not yet reached. They dismounted there. With his hand he smoothed a place in its shade where the Prophet ﷺ could sleep, spread a fur over it, and said, "Sleep, Messenger of Allah, and I will look about for you." The Prophet ﷺ lay down, and Abu Bakr went out to see whether any of the pursuers were in sight.

paragraphs.text: What he saw was a shepherd boy driving his sheep towards the same rock, wanting from it what they had wanted: its shade. "Whose are you, boy?" Abu Bakr asked, and the boy named his master. "Is there milk in your sheep?" "Yes." "Will you milk for me?" "Yes." The boy took hold of a ewe. Abu Bakr told him to shake the dust from its udder, then to shake the dust from his hands. When al-Bara told the story, he struck one hand against the other to show how. Then the boy milked a little milk into a wooden bowl.

paragraphs.text: ‘Aishah's report in al-Bukhari describes the guide by his clan, Banu al-Dil, and his skill, but does not name him. The name comes from Ibn Ishaq, through Asma bint Abi Bakr, who counted the travellers as four: the Prophet ﷺ, Abu Bakr, ‘Amir ibn Fuhayrah and "‘Abdullah ibn Arqat, their guide". Ibn Hisham adds, "it is also said: ‘Abdullah ibn Urayqit," the form used in this app. The modern commentator Hani Faqih notes the same: the Sahih has "a man of Banu al-Dil", and Ibn Ishaq gives the name.

in_depth.title: A guide who did not share their faith

paragraphs.text: The guide followed the religion of Quraysh, yet the two trusted him with their camels and with the secret of their route. Al-Qurtubi quotes ‘Aishah's report and two scholars' conclusions from it: al-Muhallab, that people of another faith may be trusted with secrets and property when they are known to be faithful and honourable; and Ibn al-Mundhir, that Muslims may hire them as guides.

paragraphs.text: Ibn Ishaq names the guide's route as a chain of places: below Makkah, along the coast, out onto the road below ‘Usfan, by lower Amaj, back to the road after Qudayd, then al-Kharrar, Thaniyyat al-Marrah, Liqf, and on through a series of valleys and passes to al-‘Arj, and from there to Batn Ri'm and Quba. Ibn Hisham records other spellings for several of the names, and adds that at al-‘Arj one of their mounts lagged, and a man of Aslam, Aws ibn Hujr, carried the Prophet ﷺ to Madinah on his camel. Musa ibn ‘Uqbah, in al-Bayhaqi, describes the opening of the route the same way: below Makkah, the coast below ‘Usfan, and past Qudayd.

paragraphs.text: Abu Bakr's account of the noon rest reaches us through al-Bara ibn ‘Azib, in al-Bukhari, in Muslim and in al-Bayhaqi, with small differences. Asked whose he was, the shepherd answers "so-and-so" in al-Bukhari, "a man of Madinah" in Muslim, and "a man of Quraysh", whom Abu Bakr recognised, in al-Bayhaqi. In Muslim it is the Prophet ﷺ who asks, "Has the time to leave not come?"; in al-Bayhaqi, Abu Bakr says, "The time to leave has come." Abu Bakr tells the journey from the night they left Makkah and does not mention the cave, so the reports do not say on which day of the road the noon rest fell. In all three, the pursuit follows right after it; in Muslim and al-Bayhaqi, the rider who catches up is Suraqah ibn Malik.

source_units.text: Ibn Ishaq said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stayed in the cave for three days, with Abu Bakr. When Quraysh lost track of him, they offered a hundred camels to anyone who would bring him back to them. During the day, ‘Abdullah ibn Abu Bakr would stay among Quraysh, listening to what they were planning and what they were saying about the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and Abu Bakr. At dusk, he would go to the two of them and tell them what he had heard. ‘Amir ibn Fuhayrah, Abu Bakr’s freedman, would graze with the shepherds of the people of Makkah. At dusk, he would bring Abu Bakr’s sheep to the two of them, and they would milk and slaughter from them. When ‘Abdullah ibn Abu Bakr left them in the morning for Makkah, ‘Amir ibn Fuhayrah would follow his tracks with the sheep, covering them up. When the three days had passed and people had ceased searching for them, the man they had hired came to them with their two camels and a camel of his own. Asma’ bint Abu Bakr brought them their provisions, but she had forgotten to bring a cord for tying them. When they set out, she went to hang up the provisions and found there was no cord. So she untied her waist-belt, made it into a cord, and hung them up with it.

قَالَ ابْنُ إسْحَاقَ: فَلَمَّا خَرَجَ بِهِمَا دَلِيلُهُمَا عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ أَرْقَطَ، سَلَكَ بِهِمَا أَسْفَلَ مَكَّةَ، ثُمَّ مَضَى بِهِمَا عَلَى السَّاحِلِ، حَتَّى عَارَضَ الطَّرِيقَ أَسْفَلَ مِنْ عُسْفَانَ، ثُمَّ سَلَكَ بِهِمَا عَلَى أَسْفَلِ أَمَجَ، ثُمَّ اسْتَجَازَ بِهِمَا، حَتَّى عَارَضَ بِهِمَا الطَّرِيقَ، بَعْدَ أَنْ أَجَازَ قُدَيْدًا، ثُمَّ أَجَازَ بِهِمَا مِنْ مَكَانِهِ ذَلِكَ، فَسَلَكَ بِهِمَا الْخَرَّارَ، ثُمَّ سَلَكَ بِهِمَا ثَنِيَّةَ الْمَرَّةِ، ثُمَّ سَلَكَ بِهِمَا لِقْفا.
قَالَ ابْنُ هِشَامٍ: وَيُقَالُ، لَفْتَا. قَالَ مَعْقِلُ بْنُ خُوَيْلِدٍ الْهُذَلِيُّ:
نَزِيعًا مُحْلِبًا مِنْ أَهْلِ لَفْتٍ ... لِحَيٍّ بَيْنَ أَثْلَةَ وَالنِّحَامِ
قَالَ ابْنُ إسْحَاقَ: ثُمَّ أَجَازَ بِهِمَا مَدْلَجَةَ لِقْفٍ ثُمَّ اسْتَبْطَنَ بِهِمَا مَدْلَجَةَ مَحَاجَّ- وَيُقَالُ: مِجَاجٍ [١]، فِيمَا قَالَ ابْنُ هِشَامٍ- ثُمَّ سَلَكَ بِهِمَا مَرْجِحَ مَحَاجَّ، ثُمَّ تَبَطَّنَ بِهِمَا مَرْجِحَ مِنْ ذِي الْغَضْوَيْنِ- قَالَ ابْنُ هِشَامٍ: وَيُقَالُ: الْعُضْوَيْنِ- ثُمَّ بَطْنَ ذِي كَشْرٍ [٢]، ثُمَّ أَخَذَ بِهِمَا عَلَى الْجَدَاجِدِ، ثُمَّ عَلَى الْأَجْرَدِ، ثُمَّ سَلَكَ بِهِمَا ذَا سَلَمٍ، مِنْ بَطْنِ أَعْدَاءِ مَدْلِجَةٍ تِعْهِنِ [٣]، ثُمَّ عَلَى الْعَبَابِيدِ. قَالَ ابْنُ هِشَامٍ:
وَيُقَالُ: الْعَبَابِيبُ، وَيُقَالُ: الْعِثْيَانَةَ. يُرِيدُ: الْعَبَابِيبَ-.
قَالَ ابْنُ إسْحَاقَ: ثُمَّ أَجَازَ بِهِمَا الْفَاجَّةَ، وَيُقَالُ: الْقَاحَّةُ، فِيمَا قَالَ ابْنُ هِشَامٍ.
قَالَ ابْنُ هِشَامٍ: ثُمَّ هَبَطَ بِهِمَا الْعَرْجَ، وَقَدْ أَبْطَأَ عَلَيْهِمَا بَعْضُ ظَهْرِهِمْ، فَحَمَلَ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ﷺ رَجُلٌ مِنْ أَسْلَمَ، يُقَالُ لَهُ: أَوْسُ بْنُ حُجْرٍ، عَلَى جَمَلٍ لَهُ- يُقَالُ لَهُ: ابْنُ الرِّدَاءِ- إلَى الْمَدِينَةِ، وَبَعَثَ مَعَهُ غُلَامًا لَهُ، يُقَالُ لَهُ:

Ibn Ishaq said: When their guide, ‘Abdullah ibn Urayqit, set out with the two of them, he took them along the lower part of Makkah, then continued with them along the coast until he joined the road below ‘Usfan. Then he took them along the lower part of Amaj, and continued until he joined the road after passing through Qudayd. From there he went on with them along al-Kharrar, then along the mountain pass of al-Marra, then along Liqfa.

Ibn Hisham said: It is also said to be Lafta. Ma‘qil ibn Khuwailid al-Hudhali said:

“A man of noble descent, bringing milk from the people of Laft,
for a clan between Athlah and al-Niham.”

Ibn Ishaq said: Then he took them through the pass of Liqf, then through the narrow valley of Mahaj—called Mijaj, according to Ibn Hisham. Then he traveled with them along the route of Mahaj, then through the route from Dhu al-Ghadwayn—called al-‘Udhwayn, according to Ibn Hisham—then through the valley of Dhu Kashr. Then he took them along al-Jadājid, then al-Ajrad, then along Dhu Salam, from the valley of the enemies of the narrow valley of Ti‘hin, then along al-‘Ababid. Ibn Hisham said: It is also said al-‘Ababib, and al-‘Uthyanah; what is meant is al-‘Ababib.

Ibn Ishaq said: Then he took them through al-Fajj—called al-Qahhah, according to Ibn Hisham.

Ibn Hisham said: Then he brought them down to al-‘Arj. Some of their mounts had fallen behind, so a man from the tribe of Aslam, called Aws ibn Hajr, carried the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to Madinah on a camel of his called Ibn al-Rida’. He sent along with him a young servant of his, called…

source_units.text_ar: <hadeeth-1487>«أَقْبَلَ نَبِيُّ اللهِ ﷺ إِلَى الْمَدِينَةِ وَهْوَ مُرْدِفٌ، أَبَا بَكْرٍ وَأَبُو بَكْرٍ شَيْخٌ يُعْرَفُ، وَنَبِيُّ اللهِ ﷺ شَابٌّ لَا يُعْرَفُ، قَالَ: فَيَلْقَى الرَّجُلُ أَبَا بَكْرٍ فَيَقُولُ: يَا أَبَا بَكْرٍ، مَنْ هَذَا الرَّجُلُ الَّذِي بَيْنَ يَدَيْكَ؟ فَيَقُولُ: هَذَا الرَّجُلُ يَهْدِينِي السَّبِيلَ. قَالَ: فَيَحْسِبُ الْحَاسِبُ أَنَّهُ إِنَّمَا يَعْنِي الطَّرِيقَ، وَإِنَّمَا يَعْنِي سَبِيلَ الْخَيْرِ. فَالْتَفَتَ أَبُو بَكْرٍ فَإِذَا هُوَ بِفَارِسٍ قَدْ لَحِقَهُمْ، فَقَالَ: يَا رَسُولَ اللهِ، هَذَا فَارِسٌ قَدْ لَحِقَ بِنَا. فَالْتَفَتَ نَبِيُّ اللهِ ﷺ فَقَالَ: اللَّهُمَّ اصْرَعْهُ فَصَرَعَهُ الْفَرَسُ، ثُمَّ قَامَتْ تُحَمْحِمُ، فَقَالَ: يَا نَبِيَّ اللهِ، مُرْنِي بِمَ شِئْتَ، قَالَ: فَقِفْ مَكَانَكَ، لَا تَتْرُكَنَّ أَحَدًا يَلْحَقُ بِنَا قَالَ: فَكَانَ أَوَّلَ النَّهَارِ جَاهِدًا عَلَى نَبِيِّ اللهِ ﷺ، وَكَانَ آخِرَ النَّهَارِ مَسْلَحَةً لَهُ، فَنَزَلَ رَسُولُ اللهِ ﷺ جَانِبَ الْحَرَّةِ، ثُمَّ بَعَثَ إِلَى الْأَنْصَارِ فَجَاؤُوا إِلَى نَبِيِّ اللهِ ﷺ فَسَلَّمُوا عَلَيْهِمَا، وَقَالُوا: ارْكَبَا آمِنَيْنِ مُطَاعَيْنِ. فَرَكِبَ نَبِيُّ اللهِ ﷺ وَأَبُو بَكْرٍ، وَحَفُّوا دُونَهُمَا بِالسِّلَاحِ، فَقِيلَ فِي الْمَدِينَةِ: جَاءَ نَبِيُّ اللهِ، جَاءَ نَبِيُّ اللهِ ﷺ، فَأَشْرَفُوا يَنْظُرُونَ وَيَقُولُونَ: جَاءَ نَبِيُّ اللهِ، جَاءَ نَبِيُّ اللهِ، فَأَقْبَلَ يَسِيرُ حَتَّى نَزَلَ جَانِبَ دَارِ أَبِي أَيُّوبَ، فَإِنَّهُ لَيُحَدِّثُ أَهْلَهُ إِذْ سَمِعَ بِهِ عَبْدُ اللهِ<hadeeth>

source_units.text: “The Prophet of God ﷺ approached Medina with Abu Bakr riding behind him. Abu Bakr was an older man whom people recognized, while the Prophet of God ﷺ was a young man whom they did not recognize. A man would encounter Abu Bakr and ask, ‘Abu Bakr, who is this man before you?’ He would reply, ‘This man guides me along the way.’ The listener thought he meant the road, but he meant the way of goodness. Abu Bakr turned and saw a horseman who had caught up with them. He said, ‘Messenger of God, a horseman has caught up with us!’ The Prophet of God ﷺ turned and said, ‘O God, throw him down!’ His horse threw him and then rose neighing. He said, ‘Prophet of God, command me to do whatever you wish.’ He replied, ‘Stay where you are; do not let anyone catch up with us.’ Early in the day he had fought against the Prophet of God ﷺ; by the end of the day he was guarding him. The Messenger of God ﷺ stopped beside the lava tract and sent for the Ansar. They came to the Prophet of God ﷺ, greeted the two men, and said, ‘Ride on, safe and obeyed.’ The Prophet of God ﷺ and Abu Bakr rode on, and the Ansar surrounded them with weapons. People in Medina said, ‘The Prophet of God has come! The Prophet of God ﷺ has come!’ They peered out, looking and saying, ‘The Prophet of God has come! The Prophet of God has come!’ He continued until he stopped beside Abu Ayyub’s house. While he was speaking to his family, ‘Abd Allah [the name breaks off at the excerpt boundary] heard of him.”

٧٥ - (٢٠٠٩) حَدَّثَنِي سَلَمَةُ بْنُ شَبِيبٍ. حَدَّثَنَا الْحَسَنُ بْنُ أعين. حدثنا زهير. حدثنا أَبُو إِسْحَاقَ قَالَ: سَمِعْتُ الْبَرَاءَ بْنَ عَازِبٍ يقول:
جاء أبو بكر الصديق إلى أبي في منزله. فاشترى منه رحلا. فقال لعازب: ابعث معي ابنك يحمله معي إلى منزلي. فقال لي أبي: احمله. فحملته. وخرج أبي معه ينتقد ثمنه. فقال له أبي: يا أبا بكر! حدثني كيف صنعتما ليلة سريت مَعَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ ﷺ. قال: نعم. أسرينا ليلتنا كلها. حتى قام قائم الظهيرة. وخلا الطريق فلا يمر فيه أحد. حتى رفعت لنا صخرة طويلة لها ظل. لم تأت عليه الشمس بعد. فنزلنا عندها. فأتيت الصخرة فسويت بيدي مكانا. ينام فيه النبي ﷺ في ظلها. ثم بسطت عليه فروة. ثم قلت: نم.
source_units.speaker_ar: مسلم عن البراء عن أبي بكر
source_units.text:
75 - (2009) Salamah ibn Shabib told me: al-Hasan ibn A‘yan told us: Zuhayr told us: Abu Ishaq told us. He said: I heard al-Bara’ ibn ‘Azib say:
Abu Bakr al-Siddiq came to my father’s house and bought a saddle from him. He said to ‘Azib, “Send your son with me to carry it to my home.” My father said to me, “Carry it.” So I carried it, and my father went with him to collect the price. My father said to him, “Abu Bakr, tell me how you spent the night traveling with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.” He replied, “Certainly. We traveled through the whole night until midday, when the road was empty and no one passed along it. Then a tall rock with a patch of shade came into view, untouched by the sun. We stopped there. I went to the rock and smoothed a place with my hands for the Prophet ﷺ to sleep in its shade. Then I spread a fur over it and said, ‘Sleep.’”

source_units.text_ar: يا رسول الله! وأنا أنفض لك ما حولك. فنام. وخرجت أنفض ما حوله. فإذا أنا براعي غنم مقبل بغنمه إلى الصخرة، يريد منها الذي أردنا. فلقيته فقلت: لمن أنت؟ يا غلام! فقال: لرجل من أهل المدينة. قلت: أفي غنمك لبن؟ قال: نعم. قلت: أفتحلب لي؟ قال: نعم. فأخذ شاة. فقلت له: انفض الضرع من الشعر والتراب والقذى (قال فرأيت البراء يضرب بيده على الأخرى ينفض) فحلب لي، في قعب معه، كثبة من لبن. قال ومعي إدواة أرتوي فيها للنبي ﷺ، ليشرب منها ويتوضأ. قَالَ فَأَتَيْتُ النَّبِيَّ ﷺ. وكرهت أن أوقظه من نومه. فوافقته استيقظ. فصببت على اللبن من الماء حتى برد أسفله. فقلت: يا رسول الله! اشرب من هذا اللبن. قال فشرب حتى رضيت. ثم قال "ألم يأن للرحيل؟ " قلت: بلى. قال فارتحلنا بعد ما زالت الشمس. واتبعنا سراقة بن مالك. قال ونحن في جلد من الأرض. فقلت: يا رسول الله! أتينا. فقال "لا تحزن إن الله معنا" فَدَعَا عَلَيْهِ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ. فارتطمت فرسه إلى بطنها. أرى فقال: إني قد علمت أنكما قد دعوتما علي. فادعوا لي. فالله لكما أن أرد عنكما الطلب. فدعا الله. فنجى. فرجع لا يلقى أحدا إلا قال: قد كفيتكم ما ههنا. فلا يلقى أحدا إلا رده. قال ووفى لنا.
source_units.speaker_ar: أبو بكر في رواية البراء عند مسلم
source_units.text: “Messenger of Allah, I’ll clear away what is around you.” He slept, and I went out to clear the area around him. Then I saw a shepherd coming with his sheep toward the rock, wanting what we wanted from it. I met him and asked, “Whom do you belong to, young man?” He said, “A man from Madinah.” I asked, “Do your sheep have milk?” He said, “Yes.” I asked, “Will you milk one for me?” He said, “Yes.” He took a ewe. I said, “Shake the udder free of hair, dirt, and debris.” (Al-Bara’ said, “I saw him strike one hand against the other to shake it off.”) He milked some milk for me into a bowl he had with him. I had a waterskin in which I had set aside water for the Prophet ﷺ to drink and perform ablution. I came to the Prophet ﷺ, and I did not want to wake him from his sleep. But when I arrived, he had woken up. I poured water onto the milk until the bottom of it had cooled. I said, “Messenger of Allah, drink some of this milk.” He drank until I was satisfied. Then he said, “Isn’t it time to set out?” I said, “Yes.” We set out after the sun had passed its zenith. Suraqah ibn Malik pursued us. We were crossing a stretch of bare land. I said, “Messenger of Allah, they have caught up with us!” He said, “Do not grieve; Allah is with us.” The Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed against him, and his horse sank up to its belly. I think he said, “I know that you two have prayed against me. Pray for me, and I pledge to Allah that I will turn away those pursuing you.” He prayed to Allah, and Suraqah was delivered. He went back, and whenever he met anyone, he said, “I have dealt with what is ahead of you,” and turned them back. He kept his pledge to us.

source_units.text_ar: ٣٩١٧ - حَدَّثَنَا أَحْمَدُ بْنُ عُثْمَانَ: حَدَّثَنَا شُرَيْحُ بْنُ مَسْلَمَةَ: حَدَّثَنَا إِبْرَاهِيمُ بْنُ يُوسُفَ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ، عَنْ أَبِي إِسْحَاقَ قَالَ: سَمِعْتُ الْبَرَاءَ يُحَدِّثُ قَالَ: «ابْتَاعَ أَبُو بَكْرٍ مِنْ عَازِبٍ رَحْلًا، فَحَمَلْتُهُ مَعَهُ، قَالَ: فَسَأَلَهُ عَازِبٌ، عَنْ مَسِيرِ رَسُولِ اللهِ ﷺ، قَالَ: أُخِذَ عَلَيْنَا بِالرَّصَدِ، فَخَرَجْنَا لَيْلًا، فَأَحْثَثْنَا لَيْلَتَنَا وَيَوْمَنَا حَتَّى قَامَ قَائِمُ الظَّهِيرَةِ، ثُمَّ رُفِعَتْ لَنَا صَخْرَةٌ، فَأَتَيْنَاهَا وَلَهَا شَيْءٌ مِنْ ظِلٍّ، قَالَ: فَفَرَشْتُ لِرَسُولِ اللهِ ﷺ فَرْوَةً مَعِي، ثُمَّ اضْطَجَعَ عَلَيْهَا النَّبِيُّ ﷺ، فَانْطَلَقْتُ أَنْفُضُ مَا حَوْلَهُ، فَإِذَا أَنَا بِرَاعٍ قَدْ أَقْبَلَ فِي غُنَيْمَةٍ يُرِيدُ مِنَ الصَّخْرَةِ مِثْلَ الَّذِي أَرَدْنَا، فَسَأَلْتُهُ: لِمَنْ أَنْتَ يَا غُلَامُ؟ فَقَالَ: أَنَا لِفُلَانٍ، فَقُلْتُ لَهُ: هَلْ فِي غَنَمِكَ مِنْ لَبَنٍ؟ قَالَ: نَعَمْ، قُلْتُ لَهُ: هَلْ أَنْتَ حَالِبٌ؟ قَالَ: نَعَمْ، فَأَخَذَ شَاةً مِنْ غَنَمِهِ، فَقُلْتُ لَهُ: انْفُضِ الضَّرْعَ، قَالَ: فَحَلَبَ كُثْبَةً مِنْ لَبَنٍ، وَمَعِي إِدَاوَةٌ مِنْ مَاءٍ عَلَيْهَا خِرْقَةٌ، قَدْ رَوَّأْتُهَا لِرَسُولِ اللهِ ﷺ، فَصَبَبْتُ عَلَى اللَّبَنِ حَتَّى بَرَدَ أَسْفَلُهُ، ثُمَّ أَتَيْتُ بِهِ النَّبِيَّ ﷺ فَقُلْتُ: اشْرَبْ يَا رَسُولَ اللهِ، فَشَرِبَ رَسُولُ اللهِ ﷺ حَتَّى رَضِيتُ، ثُمَّ ارْتَحَلْنَا وَالطَّلَبُ فِي إِثْرِنَا، ٣٩١٨ - قَالَ الْبَرَاءُ: فَدَخَلْتُ مَعَ أَبِي بَكْرٍ عَلَى أَهْلِهِ، فَإِذَا عَائِشَةُ ابْنَتُهُ مُضْطَجِعَةٌ قَدْ أَصَابَتْهَا حُمَّى، فَرَأَيْتُ
source_units.speaker_ar: البراء عن أبي بكر في المسير؛ ثم مشاهدة البراء لعيادة عائشة
source_units.text: 3917 - Ahmad ibn ‘Uthman told us: Shurayh ibn Maslamah told us: Ibrahim ibn Yusuf told us, from his father, from Abu Ishaq, who said: I heard al-Bara’ relate: “Abu Bakr bought a saddle from ‘Azib, and I carried it with him. ‘Azib asked him about the journey of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He said, ‘They had set watchers on us, so we left at night and traveled swiftly throughout the night and the day, until midday. Then a rock came into view, and we went to it; it had some shade. I spread out a fur I had with me for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and the Prophet ﷺ lay down on it. I went off to clear the area around him, and then I saw a shepherd approaching with a small flock, heading for the rock for the same reason we were. I asked him, “Whom do you belong to, young man?” He said, “I belong to so-and-so.” I asked him, “Do your sheep have any milk?” He said, “Yes.” I asked him, “Will you milk one?” He said, “Yes.” He took a ewe from his flock. I said to him, “Shake the udder.” He milked some milk, and I had a waterskin of water with a cloth over it, which I had set aside for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. I poured it onto the milk until the bottom of it had cooled. Then I brought it to the Prophet ﷺ and said, “Drink, Messenger of Allah.” The Messenger of Allah ﷺ drank until I was satisfied. Then we set out, with the pursuers on our trail.’ 3918 - Al-Bara’ said: ‘I went with Abu Bakr into his family’s home, and there was his daughter ‘Aishah lying down, afflicted with a fever. I saw—’”

source_units.text_ar:
فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ: إنِّي لَا أَرْكَبُ بَعِيرًا لَيْسَ لِي، قَالَ: فَهِيَ لَكَ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ، بِأَبِي أَنْتَ وَأُمِّي، قَالَ: لَا، وَلَكِنْ مَا الثَّمَنُ الَّذِي ابْتَعْتهَا بِهِ؟ قَالَ:
كَذَا وَكَذَا، قَالَ: قَدْ أَخَذْتهَا بِهِ، قَالَ: هِيَ لَكَ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ [١] . فَرَكِبَا وَانْطَلَقَا وَأَرْدَفَ أَبُو بَكْرٍ الصِّدِّيقُ ﵁ عَامِرَ بْنَ فُهَيْرَةَ مَوْلَاهُ خَلْفَهُ، لِيَخْدِمَهُمَا فِي الطَّرِيقِ.
source_units.speaker_ar: ابن إسحاق
source_units.text: The Messenger of God ﷺ replied, “I do not ride a camel that is not mine.” He said, “Then it is yours, Messenger of God, may my father and mother be your ransom.” He said, “No. What price did you buy it for?” He said, “Such and such.” He said, “I have taken it for that price.” He replied, “It is yours, Messenger of God [1].” They mounted and departed, and Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may God be pleased with him, took his freedman ‘Amir ibn Fuhayra riding behind him to serve them on the road.

source_units.text_ar: ثُمَّ انْطَلَقَا وَانْطَلَقَا مَعَهُمَا بِعَامِرِ بْنِ فُهَيْرَةَ يَخْدُمُهُمَا وَيُعِينُهُمَا، يُرْدِفُهُ أَبُو بَكْرٍ، وَيُعْقِبُهُ عَلَى رَاحِلَتِهِ، لَيْسَ مَعَهُمَا أَحَدٌ مِنَ النَّاسِ غَيْرُ عَامِرِ بْنِ فُهَيْرَةَ، وَغَيْرُ أَخِي بَنِي عدي يديهما الطَّرِيقَ فَأَجَازَ بِهِمَا أَسْفَلَ مَكَّةَ ثُمَّ مَضَى بِهِمَا السَّاحِلَ أَسْفَلَ مِنْ عُسْفَانَ ثُمَّ أَجَازَ بِهِمَا حَتَّى عَارَضَ الطَّرِيقَ بَعْدَ أَنْ أَجَازَ قُدَيْدًا» [(٢٧)] .
source_units.kind_ar: تتمة النقل بعد تمييز مدة موسى، مع تعقيب البيهقي على اللفظ والمعنى
source_units.speaker_ar: النقل المقارن لعروة وموسى كما يورده البيهقي؛ لا نسبة حصرية لألفاظ التتمة إلى موسى
source_units.text: Then the two set out, taking ‘Amir ibn Fuhayrah with them to serve and assist them. Abu Bakr let him ride behind him and took turns with him on his mount. No one accompanied them except ‘Amir ibn Fuhayrah and a guide from Banu ‘Adi. The guide led them along the road and took them through the lower part of Makkah. Then he went with them along the coast, south of ‘Usfan, and continued until he joined the main road after taking them past Qudayd.”

source_units.text_ar:
فَلَا يَسْمَعُ أَمْرًا يَكِيدُونَ [(٢١)] بِهِ إِلَّا وَعَاهُ حَتَّى يَأْتِيَهُمَا بِخَبَرِ ذَلِكَ حِينَ يَخْتَلِطُ الظَّلَامَ، وَيَرْعَى عَلَيْهِمَا عَامِرُ بْنُ فُهَيْرَةَ [(٢٢)] مَوْلَى أَبِي بَكْرٍ مِنْحَةً مِنْ غَنَمٍ فَيَرِيحُ عَلَيْهِمَا حِينَ تَذْهَبُ سَاعَةٌ مِنَ اللَّيْلِ فَيَبِيتَانِ فِي رِسْلِ مِنْحَتِهِمَا وَرَضِيفِهِمَا، حَتَّى يَنْعِقَ بِهِمَا عَامِرُ بْنُ فُهَيْرَةَ بِغَلَسٍ، يَفْعَلُ ذَلِكَ كُلَّ لَيْلَةٍ مِنْ تِلْكَ اللَّيَالِي الثَّلَاثِ.
وَاسْتَأْجَرَ، رَسُولُ اللهِ ﵌ وَأَبُو بَكْرٍ رَجُلًا مِنْ بَنِي الدِّيلِ مِنْ بَنِي عَبْدِ بْنِ عَدِيِّ هَادِيًا خِرِّيتًا [(٢٣)] وَالْخِرِّيتُ الْمَاهِرُ بِالْهِدَايَةِ قَدْ غَمَسَ حِلْفًا فِي آلِ الْعَاصِ بْنِ وَائِلٍ، وَهُوَ عَلَى دِينِ كُفَّارِ قُرَيْشٍ، فَأَمِنَاهُ فَدَفَعَا إِلَيْهِ رَاحِلَتَيْهِمَا، وَوَاعَدَاهُ غَارَ ثَوْرٍ فَأَتَاهُمَا بِرَاحِلَتَيْهِمَا صَبِيحَةَ ثَلَاثِ لَيَالٍ، فَارْتَحَلَا وَانْطَلَقَ عَامِرُ بْنُ فُهَيْرَةَ وَالدَّلِيلُ الدُّؤَلِيُّ فَأَخَذَ بِهِمَا يَدَ بَحْرٍ وَهُوَ طَرِيقُ السَّاحِلِ» .
source_units.speaker_ar: عائشة برواية عروة والزهري
source_units.text:
He would hear any plan they devised against them and memorize it, then bring them news of it when darkness fell. ‘Amir ibn Fuhayrah, Abu Bakr’s freedman, grazed a flock of sheep for them. After an hour of the night had passed, he brought the sheep to them, and they spent the night drinking their milk and warming themselves with heated stones, until ‘Amir ibn Fuhayrah called them at the break of dawn. He did this each night during those three nights.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ and Abu Bakr hired a man from Banu al-Dayl, of Banu ‘Abd ibn ‘Adiy, as a skilled guide. A skilled guide is one who is adept at finding the way. He had made an alliance with the family of al-‘As ibn Wa’il and followed the religion of Quraysh’s unbelievers, but they trusted him. They handed him their two mounts and arranged to meet him at the Cave of Thawr. He brought their mounts to them on the morning of the third night. They set out, and ‘Amir ibn Fuhayrah and the Dalite guide went with them, taking the coastal route.”

source_units.text_ar: قَوْلُهُ: (وَأَبُو بَكْرٍ شَيْخٌ) يُرِيدُ أَنَّهُ قَدْ شَابَ، وَقَوْلُهُ: يُعْرَفُ أَيْ لِأَنَّهُ كَانَ يَمُرُّ عَلَى أَهْلِ الْمَدِينَةِ فِي سَفَرِ التِّجَارَةِ، بِخِلَافِ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ فِي الْأَمْرَيْنِ فَإِنَّهُ كَانَ بَعِيدَ الْعَهْدِ بِالسَّفَرِ مِنْ مَكَّةَ، وَلَمْ يَشِبْ، وَإِلَّا فَفِي نَفْسِ الْأَمْرِ كَانَ هُوَ ﵊ أَسَنَّ مِنْ أَبِي بَكْرٍ، وَسَيَأْتِي فِي هَذَا الْبَابِ مِنْ حَدِيثِ أَنَسٍ
source_units.speaker_ar: ابن حجر العسقلاني؛ النقول المسماة في كلامه لأصحابها
source_units.book_ar: فتح الباري بشرح البخاري - ط السلفية
source_units.text: His saying, “Abu Bakr was an old man,” means that his hair had turned gray. The statement that he “was recognized” means that he used to pass through Madinah on trading journeys. The Prophet ﷺ differed from him in both respects: he had not traveled from Makkah for a long time, and his hair had not turned gray. In reality, however, he ﷺ was older than Abu Bakr. A report from Anas will appear in this chapter.

source_units.text_ar:
أَنَّهُ لَمْ يَكُنْ فِي الَّذِينَ هَاجَرُوا أَشْمَطَ غَيْرَ أَبِي بَكْرٍ.
قَوْلُهُ: (وَنَبِيُّ اللَّهِ شَابٌّ لَا يُعْرَفُ) ظَاهِرُهُ أَنَّ أَبَا بَكْرٍ كَانَ أَسَنَّ مِنَ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ وَلَيْسَ كَذَلِكَ،
source_units.kind_ar: تتمة كلام ابن حجر عن الشمط ونقد ظاهر الشيخ والشاب
source_units.speaker_ar: ابن حجر
source_units.book_ar: فتح الباري بشرح البخاري - ط السلفية
source_units.text: Among those who emigrated, Abu Bakr was the only one with gray hair. His statement, “The Prophet of Allah was a young man, not known to be [older],” apparently means that Abu Bakr was older than the Prophet ﷺ, but that is not so.

source_units.text_ar: قُلْتُ: وَهُوَ كَمَا ظَنَّ، وَإِنَّمَا يُعْرَفُ هَذَا لِلْعَبَّاسِ، وَأَمَّا أَبُو بَكْرٍ فَثَبَتَ فِي صَحِيحِ مُسْلِمٍ، عَنْ مُعَاوِيَةَ أَنَّهُ عَاشَ ثَلَاثًا وَسِتِّينَ سَنَةً، وَكَانَ قَدْ عَاشَ بَعْدَ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ سَنَتَيْنِ وَأَشْهُرًا فَيَلْزَمُ عَلَى الصَّحِيحِ فِي سِنِّ أَبِي بَكْرٍ أَنْ يَكُونَ أَصْغَرَ مِنَ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ بِأَكْثَرَ مِنْ سَنَتَيْنِ.
source_units.kind_ar: موافقة ابن حجر ونقده وحساب السن المنقول
source_units.speaker_ar: ابن حجر؛ يعزو خبرًا إلى مسلم عن معاوية
source_units.book_ar: فتح الباري بشرح البخاري - ط السلفية
source_units.text: I say: He was as he supposed, but this is known only of al-‘Abbas. As for Abu Bakr, it is established in Sahih Muslim, from Mu‘awiyah, that he lived for sixty-three years. He lived for two years and some months after the Prophet ﷺ, so, according to the soundest view of Abu Bakr’s age, he must have been more than two years younger than the Prophet ﷺ.

source_units.text_ar: أَخْبَرَنَا أَبُو الْحَسَنِ عَلِيُّ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ عَبْدَانَ، قَالَ: أَخْبَرَنَا أَحْمَدُ بْنُ عُبَيْدٍ، قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا ابْنُ أَبِي قُمَاشٍ، قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا سَعِيدُ بْنُ سُلَيْمَانَ الْوَاسِطِيُّ بِبَغْدَادَ، عَنْ أَبِي مَعْشَرٍ، عَنْ أَبِي وَهْبٍ، مَوْلَى أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ، عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ، قَالَ
source_units.speaker_ar: رواة السند إلى أبي هريرة في عرض البيهقي
source_units.text: Abu al-Hasan ‘Ali ibn Ahmad ibn ‘Abdan informed us; he said: Ahmad ibn ‘Ubayd informed us; he said: Ibn Abi Qumash told us; he said: Sa‘id ibn Sulayman al-Wasiti told us in Baghdad, from Abu Ma‘shar, from Abu Wahb, the freedman of Abu Hurayra, from Abu Hurayra, who said:

source_units.text_ar: «قَالَ رَسُولُ اللهِ ﵌ لِأَبِي بَكْرٍ فِي مُدْخَلِهِ الْمَدِينَةِ: أَلْهِ النَّاسَ عني فإنه لا
source_units.kind_ar: ابتداء متن أبي هريرة المنقطع عند حد الصفحة
source_units.speaker_ar: أبو هريرة ينقل قول النبي ﷺ لأبي بكر
source_units.text: “The Messenger of God ﷺ said to Abu Bakr on entering Medina, ‘Distract the people from me, for it is not

source_units.text_ar: يَنْبَغِي لِنَبِيٍّ أَنْ يَكْذِبَ، قَالَ: فَكَانَ أَبُو بَكْرٍ إِذَا سُئِلَ مَا أَنْتَ؟ قال: باع، فَإِذَا قِيلَ: مَنِ الَّذِي مَعَكَ؟ قَالَ: هَادٍ يَهْدِينِي»
source_units.kind_ar: تتمة متن أبي هريرة وجواب أبي بكر
source_units.speaker_ar: أبو هريرة يروي جواب أبي بكر
source_units.text: fitting for a prophet to lie.’ He said: When Abu Bakr was asked, ‘What are you?’ he replied, “bāʿ” [translator’s note: the supplied Arabic is an active past verb, literally “he sold”; its intended answer to “What are you?” is unclear]. When asked, ‘Who is with you?’ he said, ‘A guide who guides me.’”

source_units.text_ar:
أَخْبَرَنَا أَبُو الْحُسَيْنِ: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ الْحُسَيْنِ الْقَطَّانُ بِبَغْدَادَ، وقَالَ: أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ اللَّه بْنُ جَعْفَرِ بْنِ دُرُسْتَوَيْهِ، قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يَعْقُوبُ بْنُ سُفْيَانَ، قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا عُبَيْدُ اللَّه بْنُ مُوسَى، وَعَبْدُ اللَّه بْنُ رَجَاءٍ: أَبُو عُمَرَ الْغُدَانِيُّ، عَنْ إِسْرَائِيلَ، عَنْ أَبِي إِسْحَاقَ، عَنِ الْبَرَاءِ، قَالَ: «اشْتَرَى أَبُو بَكْرٍ مِنْ عَازِبٍ رَحْلًا بِثَلَاثَةَ عَشَرَ دِرْهَمًا، فَقَالَ أَبُو بَكْرٍ ﵁ لِعَازِبٍ: مُرِ الْبَرَاءَ فَلْيَحْمِلْهُ إِلَى رَحْلِي، فَقَالَ لَهُ عَازِبٌ: لَا، حَتَّى تُحَدِّثَنَا كَيْفَ صَنَعْتَ أَنْتَ وَرَسُولُ اللَّه ﵌ حِينَ خَرَجْتُمَا وَالْمُشْرِكُونَ يَطْلُبُونَكُمَا قَالَ: أَدْلَجْنَا مِنْ مَكَّةَ لَيْلًا، فَأَحْيَيْنَا لَيْلَتَنَا وَيَوْمَنَا حَتَّى أَظْهَرْنَا، وَقَامَ قَائِمُ الظَّهِيرَةِ، فَرَمَيْتُ بِبَصَرِي هَلْ أَرَى مِنْ ظِلٍّ نَأْوِي إِلَيْهِ فَإِذَا صَخْرَةٌ، فَانْتَهَيْتُ إِلَيْهَا، فَإِذَا بَقِيَّةُ ظِلٍّ لَهَا، فَسَوَّيْتُهُ، ثُمَّ فَرَشْتُ لِرَسُولِ اللَّه ﵌ فَرْوَةً، ثُمَّ قُلْتُ: اضْطَجِعْ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّه، فَاضْطَجَعَ، ثُمَّ ذَهَبْتُ أَنْفُضُ مَا حَوْلِي هَلْ أَرَى مِنَ الطَّلَبِ أَحَدًا، فَإِذَا بِرَاعِي غَنَمٍ يَسُوقُ غَنَمَهُ إِلَى الصَّخْرَةِ يُرِيدُ مِنْهَا الَّذِي نُرِيدُ- يَعْنِي الظِّلَّ- فَسَأَلْتُهُ فَقُلْتُ: لِمَنْ أَنْتَ يَا غُلَامُ؟ فَقَالَ: لِرَجُلٍ مِنْ قُرَيْشٍ، فَسَمَّاهُ، فَعَرَفْتُهُ، فَقُلْتُ: هَلْ فِي غَنَمِكَ مِنْ لَبَنٍ، قَالَ: نَعَمْ، قُلْتُ:
هَلْ أَنْتَ حَالِبٌ لِي، قَالَ: نَعَمْ، فَأَمَرْتُهُ فَاعْتَقَلَ شَاةً مِنْ غَنَمِهِ، وَأَمَرْتُهُ أَنْ يَنْفُضَ ضَرْعَهَا مِنَ التُّرَابِ، ثُمَّ أَمَرْتُهُ أَنْ يَنْفُضَ كَفَّيْهِ، فَقَالَ: هَكَذَا، فَضَرَبَ إِحْدَى كَفَّيْهِ عَلَى الْأُخْرَى، فَحَلَبَ لِي كُثْبَةً [(١)] مِنْ لَبَنٍ وَقَدْ رَوَيْتُ مَعِي لِرَسُولِ اللَّه
source_units.speaker_ar: أبو بكر برواية البراء
source_units.text: Abu al-Husayn Muhammad ibn al-Husayn al-Qattan in Baghdad informed us, saying: ‘Abdullah ibn Ja‘far ibn Durustawayh informed us, saying: Ya‘qub ibn Sufyan narrated to us, saying: ‘Ubaydullah ibn Musa and ‘Abdullah ibn Raja’, Abu ‘Umar al-Ghudani, narrated to us, from Isra’il, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Bara’, who said: “Abu Bakr bought a saddle from ‘Azib for thirteen dirhams. Abu Bakr said to ‘Azib: ‘Tell al-Bara’ to carry it to my saddle.’ ‘Azib said to him: ‘No, not until you tell us what you and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did when you set out and the polytheists were pursuing you.’ He said: ‘We left Makkah at night and traveled through the night and the day until the afternoon. When the midday heat set in, I looked around to see whether there was any shade where we could take shelter. I saw a rock and went to it. There was a patch of shade beside it, so I leveled it. Then I spread a fur for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: “Lie down, Messenger of Allah.” He lay down. Then I went off, looking around me to see whether I could spot any pursuers. Suddenly I saw a shepherd driving his sheep toward the rock, seeking the same thing we were—the shade. I asked him, “Whose shepherd are you, young man?” He said, “A man from Quraysh,” and named him. I recognized the man and asked, “Do any of your sheep have milk?” He said, “Yes.” I asked, “Will you milk one for me?” He said, “Yes.” I told him to catch a sheep from his flock and shake the dust from its udder. Then I told him to shake his hands. He said, “Like this?” and struck one hand against the other. He milked a small amount of milk for me. I had brought a water-skin for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, with a cloth over its opening. I poured water over the milk until the bottom of the container was cool. Then I went to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and found that he had woken up. I said, “Will you drink, Messenger of Allah?” The Messenger of Allah ﷺ drank until I was satisfied. Then I said, “It is time to set out, Messenger of Allah.”’

﵌ إِدَاوَةً عَلَى فَمِهَا خِرْقَةٌ، فَصَبَبْتُ عَلَى اللَّبَنِ حَتَّى بَرُدَ أَسْفَلُهُ، فَأَتَيْتُ رَسُولَ اللَّه ﵌، فَوَافَقْتُهُ وَقَدِ اسْتَيْقَظَ، فَقُلْتُ: أَتَشْرَبُ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّه؟ فَشَرِبَ رَسُولُ اللَّه ﵌، حَتَّى رَضِيتُ، ثُمَّ قُلْتُ: قَدْ آنَ الرَّحِيلُ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّه.
قَالَ: فَارْتَحَلْنَا وَالْقَوْمُ يَطْلُبُونَنَا، فَلَمْ يُدْرِكْنَا أَحَدٌ مِنْهُمْ غَيْرُ سُرَاقَةَ بن مالك ابن جُعْشُمٍ عَلَى فَرَسٍ لَهُ فَقُلْتُ هَذَا الطَّلَبُ قَدْ لَحِقَنَا يَا رَسُولَ اللَّه، قَالَ: لَا تَحْزَنْ، إِنَّ اللَّه مَعَنَا، فَلَمَّا أَنْ دَنَا مِنَّا وَكَانَ بَيْنَنَا وَبَيْنَهُ قِيدَ رُمْحَيْنِ أَوْ ثَلَاثَةٍ، قُلْتُ: هَذَا الطَّلَبُ قَدْ لَحِقَنَا يَا رَسُولَ اللَّه، وَبَكَيْتُ، فَقَالَ: مَا يُبْكِيكَ؟
فَقُلْتُ: أَمَا واللَّه مَا عَلَى نَفْسِي أَبْكِي، وَلَكِنِّي إِنَّمَا أَبْكِي عَلَيْكَ، قَالَ: فَدَعَا عَلَيْهِ رَسُولُ اللَّه ﵌ فَقَالَ: اللهُمَّ! اكْفِنَا بِمَا شِئْتَ، قَالَ: فَسَاخَتْ بِهِ فَرَسُهُ فِي الْأَرْضِ إِلَى بَطْنِهَا، فَوَثَبَ عَنْهَا، ثُمَّ قَالَ: يَا مُحَمَّدُ قَدْ عَلِمْتُ أَنَّ هَذَا عَمَلُكَ فَادْعُ اللَّه أَنْ تُنَجِيَنِي مِمَّا أَنَا فِيهِ، فو اللَّه لَأُعَمِّيَنَّ عَلَى مَنْ وَرَائِي مِنَ الطَّلَبِ، وَهَذِهِ كِنَانَتِي فَخُذْ مِنْهَا سَهْمًا، فَإِنَّكَ سَتَمُرُّ بِإِبِلِي وَغَنَمِي بِمَكَانِ كَذَا وَكَذَا، فَخُذْ مِنْهَا حَاجَتَكَ، فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّه ﵌: لَا حَاجَةَ لَنَا فِي إِبِلِكَ وَغَنَمِكَ، وَدَعَا لَهُ رَسُولُ اللَّه ﵌، فَانْطَلَقَ رَاجِعًا إِلَى أَصْحَابِهِ، وَمَضَى رَسُولُ اللَّه ﵌، وَأَنَا مَعَهُ حَتَّى قَدِمْنَا الْمَدِينَةَ لَيْلًا» [(٢)] .

source_units.text: He said: ‘We set out while the people were pursuing us, but none of them caught up with us except Suraqah ibn Malik ibn Ju‘shum, riding his horse. I said, “The pursuers have caught up with us, Messenger of Allah!” He said, “Do not grieve; Allah is with us.” When Suraqah drew near, and there were only two or three spear-lengths between us, I said, “The pursuers have caught up with us, Messenger of Allah!” and I wept. He said, “What makes you weep?” I replied, “By Allah, I am not weeping for myself; I am weeping only for you.” The Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed against him, saying, “O Allah, protect us from him in whatever way You will.” Suraqah’s horse sank into the ground up to its belly. He jumped off it and said, “Muhammad, I know this is your doing. Pray to Allah to rescue me from this predicament, and by Allah, I will turn away the pursuers behind me. Here is my quiver; take an arrow from it. You will pass by my camels and sheep at such-and-such a place, so take what you need from them.” The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, “We have no need of your camels or sheep.” The Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed for him, and Suraqah went back to his companions. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ and I continued until we arrived in Madinah at night.’

source_units.text: This is recorded in the Sahih (^4), but without explicitly stating his name: only a man of Banu al-Dil. Ibn Ishaq named him in the Sira (^5). It also indicates the permissibility of a Muslim seeking help from a non-Muslim in a time of need or necessity; this issue and its supporting evidence have been discussed repeatedly already.

source_units.text_ar: الْخَامِسَةُ- رَوَى الْبُخَارِيُّ عَنْ عَائِشَةَ قَالَتْ: اسْتَأْجَرَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ وَأَبُو بَكْرٍ رَجُلًا مِنْ بَنِي الدِّيلِ هَادِيًا خِرِّيتًا «٢»، وَهُوَ عَلَى دِينِ كُفَّارِ قُرَيْشٍ فَدَفَعَا إليه راحلتيهما وأعداه غَارَ ثَوْرٍ بَعْدَ ثَلَاثِ لَيَالٍ فَأَتَاهُمَا بِرَاحِلَتَيْهِمَا صَبِيحَةَ ثَلَاثٍ فَارْتَحَلَا وَارْتَحَلَ «٣» مَعَهُمَا عَامِرُ بْنُ فُهَيْرَةَ وَالدَّلِيلُ الدِّيلِيُّ فَأَخَذَ بِهِمْ طَرِيقَ السَّاحِلِ «٤».

source_units.text: Fifth: Al-Bukhari related from ‘A’isha that she said: “The Messenger of God ﷺ and Abu Bakr hired a man of Banu al-Dil as a skilled guide «2». He followed the religion of the unbelievers of Quraysh. They handed him their two mounts and appointed the cave of Thawr as their meeting place after three nights. He came to them with their mounts on the morning after three nights. They departed, as did «3» ‘Amir ibn Fuhayra and the guide of Banu al-Dil with them; he took them along the coastal route «4».”

source_units.text_ar: قَالَ الْمُهَلَّبُ: فِيهِ مِنَ الْفِقْهِ ائْتِمَانُ أَهْلِ الشِّرْكِ «٥» عَلَى السِّرِّ وَالْمَالِ إِذَا عُلِمَ مِنْهُمْ وَفَاءٌ وَمُرُوءَةٌ كَمَا ائْتَمَنَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ هَذَا الْمُشْرِكَ عَلَى سِرِّهِ فِي الْخُرُوجِ مِنْ مَكَّةَ وَعَلَى النَّاقَتَيْنِ.

source_units.text: Al-Muhallab said: A legal inference here is that polytheists «5» can be entrusted with secrets and property if they are known to be faithful and honorable, just as the Prophet ﷺ entrusted this polytheist with his secret departure from Mecca and with the two she-camels.

source_units.text: Ibn al-Mundhir said: It indicates that Muslims may hire unbelievers to guide them along the road.

source_units.text_ar: مَسْعُودُ بْنُ هُنَيْدَةَ، ثُمَّ خَرَجَ بِهِمَا دَلِيلُهُمَا مِنْ الْعَرَجِ، فَسَلَكَ بِهِمَا ثَنِيَّةَ الْعَائِرِ، عَنْ يَمِينِ رَكُوبَةٍ- وَيُقَالُ. ثَنِيَّةُ الْغَائِرِ، فِيمَا قَالَ ابْنُ هِشَامٍ- حَتَّى هَبَطَ بِهِمَا بَطْنَ رِئْمٍ، ثُمَّ قَدِمَ بِهِمَا قُبَاءٍ، عَلَى بَنِي عَمْرِو بْنِ عَوْفٍ، لِاثْنَتَيْ عَشْرَةَ لَيْلَةٍ خَلَتْ مِنْ شَهْرِ رَبِيعٍ الْأَوَّلِ يَوْمَ الِاثْنَيْنِ، حِينَ اشْتَدَّ الضَّحَاءُ، وَكَادَتْ الشَّمْسُ تَعْتَدِلُ.

questions.prompt: Who were the four riders who set out from the cave?

options.text: The Prophet ﷺ, Abu Bakr, ‘Amir ibn Fuhayrah and the guide
options.feedback: Right. Two hunted men, Abu Bakr's freedman, and a guide who did not share their faith.

options.text: The Prophet ﷺ, Abu Bakr, his son ‘Abdullah and the guide
options.feedback: ‘Abdullah had carried news to the cave, but the fourth rider was ‘Amir ibn Fuhayrah.

options.text: The Prophet ﷺ, Abu Bakr, Asma and ‘Amir ibn Fuhayrah
options.feedback: Asma brought the food bag to the cave but did not ride with them; the guide was the fourth rider.

questions.explanation: Four set out: the Prophet ﷺ, Abu Bakr, ‘Amir ibn Fuhayrah, and the hired guide; no one else went with them.

questions.prompt: How did ‘Amir ibn Fuhayrah travel on the road?

options.text: Behind Abu Bakr on his camel, at times riding it in turn
options.feedback: Right. Abu Bakr took him up behind him to serve them on the way, and at times let him ride.

options.text: On the guide's third camel, riding ahead to scout
options.feedback: The guide brought a camel of his own, but ‘Amir rode with Abu Bakr; the guide was the one who led.

options.text: On foot, driving his flock of sheep beside them
options.feedback: The sheep were for the nights at the cave; on the road ‘Amir rode behind Abu Bakr.

questions.explanation: Abu Bakr carried his freedman ‘Amir behind him on his camel, to serve them on the way, sharing the ride in turn.

questions.prompt: Which way did the guide lead them out of Makkah?

options.text: Down below Makkah, then along the coast by the edge of the sea
options.feedback: Right. He took them along the shore to the road below ‘Usfan, then by lower Amaj and through valleys and passes.

options.text: Inland through the mountain passes, keeping far from the sea
options.feedback: The road ran first along the coast, "by the edge of the sea"; the valleys and passes came after ‘Usfan.

options.text: Back past Makkah and north along the usual road
options.feedback: The guide took them down below Makkah and out along the coast, not along a road through the city.

questions.explanation: The guide led them down below Makkah and along the sea, then out past ‘Usfan and lower Amaj into the valleys beyond.

questions.prompt: Asked who rode in front of him, Abu Bakr said, "This man guides me on the way." What did he mean?

options.text: That the Prophet ﷺ guided him on the way of good
options.feedback: Right. Listeners thought he meant the road; he meant the way of good, and so he spoke no lie.

options.text: That the man was the guide they had hired for the road
options.feedback: The man in front was the Prophet ﷺ, not the hired guide, and Abu Bakr meant the way of good.

options.text: That the man was a stranger showing him a short cut
options.feedback: Abu Bakr was speaking of the Prophet ﷺ, and his words pointed to the way of good, not a road.

questions.explanation: The Prophet ﷺ had told Abu Bakr to keep people busy, for a prophet should not lie; his answer was true and hid who rode with him.

questions.prompt: Why did people on the road know Abu Bakr but not the Prophet ﷺ?

options.text: Abu Bakr had greyed and was known from his trading journeys.
options.feedback: Right. His grey hair and his trade had made him familiar; the Prophet ﷺ, whose hair had not greyed, they did not know.

options.text: Abu Bakr was much the older of the two men.
options.feedback: He looked older because his hair had greyed, but the Prophet ﷺ was in fact older, by more than two years.

options.text: The Prophet ﷺ kept his face covered on the road.
options.feedback: Nothing like this is told; people simply did not know him, while they knew Abu Bakr from his trade.

questions.explanation: Abu Bakr's grey hair and his trading journeys made him known, though the Prophet ﷺ was actually the older of the two.

questions.prompt: At the long rock one blazing noon, what did Abu Bakr do?

options.text: Spread a fur in the shade for the Prophet ﷺ to sleep, then kept watch.
options.feedback: Right. He smoothed a place with his hand, said "Sleep, Messenger of Allah", and went to look for pursuers.

options.text: Lay down beside the Prophet ﷺ while ‘Amir kept watch.
options.feedback: Abu Bakr stayed awake himself and went out to see whether any pursuers were in sight.

options.text: Urged the Prophet ﷺ to ride on before the pursuers arrived.
options.feedback: They dismounted and rested in the shade; they left only after the sun had passed its height.

questions.explanation: In the shade of the rock Abu Bakr made a resting place for the Prophet ﷺ and kept watch while he slept.

questions.prompt: How did Abu Bakr make the shepherd boy's milk fit for the Prophet ﷺ to drink?

options.text: He had the dust shaken off, then poured water over the milk to cool it.
options.feedback: Right. The boy shook the dust from the udder and his hands, and Abu Bakr cooled the milk from his flask.

options.text: He warmed the milk over a fire before bringing it.
options.feedback: No fire is mentioned; he cooled the milk with water from his leather flask.

options.text: He milked one of ‘Amir's sheep himself instead.
options.feedback: The milk came from the shepherd boy's ewe; Abu Bakr asked him to milk it.

questions.explanation: Abu Bakr took care over the milk: dust shaken off, water poured in until it was cool, and the Prophet ﷺ drank until content.

questions.prompt: How did Abu Bakr come to tell the story of the noon rest years later?

options.text: ‘Azib would not let al-Bara carry home a saddle until Abu Bakr told it.
options.feedback: Right. Abu Bakr had bought the saddle for thirteen dirhams, and ‘Azib asked how the two had fared on the road.

options.text: Suraqah asked him about it after he became Muslim.
options.feedback: The rider who caught up is the next chapter's story; this account was told to ‘Azib and his son al-Bara.

options.text: He told it in a sermon to the people of Madinah.
options.feedback: It was told privately, as the price ‘Azib asked before his son could carry the saddle home.

questions.explanation: The noon rest is known because ‘Azib made Abu Bakr tell it, and al-Bara, his son, passed it on.

questions.prompt: The guide is called ‘Abdullah ibn Urayqit. Where does his name come from?

options.text: Ibn Ishaq names him Ibn Arqat; Ibn Hisham adds "also said: Ibn Urayqit".
options.feedback: Right. Ibn Ishaq has the name through Asma; Ibn Hisham gives Urayqit as an alternative.

options.text: ‘Aishah names him in her account in al-Bukhari.
options.feedback: ‘Aishah describes him only as a skilled guide of Banu al-Dil; she does not name him.

options.text: Ibn Ishaq names him Ibn Urayqit; Ibn Hisham adds "also said: Ibn Arqat".
options.feedback: The forms are swapped: Ibn Ishaq's own form is Ibn Arqat, and Urayqit is Ibn Hisham's addition.

questions.explanation: Al-Bukhari's report leaves the guide unnamed; the name comes from Ibn Ishaq, with Ibn Hisham's variant Urayqit.

questions.prompt: What did scholars quoted by al-Qurtubi conclude from the hiring of a guide who did not share their faith?

options.text: He may be trusted with secrets and property, and hired as a guide.
options.feedback: Right. Al-Muhallab drew the trust, for one known to be faithful; Ibn al-Mundhir drew the hiring.

options.text: He must have accepted Islam before being trusted.
options.feedback: ‘Aishah's report says he followed the religion of Quraysh; the scholars drew rulings from that, not a conversion.

options.text: The hiring was a special case, with no ruling for others.
options.feedback: Both scholars drew general rulings from it: on trusting such a person and on hiring him as a guide.

questions.explanation: From ‘Aishah's report, al-Muhallab concluded such a man may be trusted, and Ibn al-Mundhir that he may be hired as a guide.

questions.prompt: Asked whose he was, how does the shepherd boy answer in the three tellings of Abu Bakr's noon story?

options.text: Al-Bukhari: "so-and-so"; Muslim: "a man of Madinah"; al-Bayhaqi: "a man of Quraysh"
options.feedback: Right. The tellings through al-Bara differ in this small detail; in al-Bayhaqi Abu Bakr knew the man.

options.text: Al-Bukhari: "a man of Quraysh"; Muslim: "so-and-so"; al-Bayhaqi: "a man of Madinah"
options.feedback: The wordings are mixed up: "so-and-so" is al-Bukhari's, and "a man of Quraysh" is al-Bayhaqi's.

options.text: All three have "a man of Quraysh", whom Abu Bakr recognised.
options.feedback: Only al-Bayhaqi has "a man of Quraysh"; al-Bukhari has "so-and-so" and Muslim "a man of Madinah".

questions.explanation: The noon story reaches us through al-Bara in three collections, which agree in substance but name the boy's master differently.
